about.title: Bucks Lake, California
about.extract: Bucks Lake is a census-designated place (CDP) in Plumas County, California, United States. Bucks Lake is located on the south shore of the lake of the same name, 13 miles (20.9 km) west-southwest in Quincy. The population was 22 at the 2020 census, up from 10 at the 2010 census.

sites.name: Hutchins
sites.operator: USDA Forest Service · Plumas National Forest
sites.about: Hutchins Group Campground is the perfect location for groups who want to explore the greater Bucks Lake area of the Plumas National Forest. This campground was severely impacted by the Dixie Fire in 2021. Timber salvage management has left the campground barren and hot so prepare by providing…

sites.name: Sundew (family Campground )
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $32 per night
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from faucets
sites.about: Sundew Campground is a great place to start your adventures at Bucks Lake. Most sites are either on the water or have a view of the water. From Sundew you can launch your kayak, stroll along the shoreline, or jump in for a swim. Larger boats can be launched at the nearby Sandy Point Day Use Area.
sites.directions: From Quincy, go west on County Road 414, to the intersection with Bucklin Road. Turn right on Bucklin Road and travel approximately 4 miles to Sundew Campground. From Oroville, go east on County…
sites.reservations: Some sites at this campground are now reservable. To reserve a site please visit visit recreation.gov Recreation.govor call 1-877-444-6777

It is an easy drive to Sandy Point Boat Launch and Day Use area on Bucks Lake. There is a short trail from the campground to Lower Bucks Lake. There is easy access to trails within…

sites.name: Lower Bucks (Family Campground)
sites.about: Lower Bucks Campground is along the north shore of Lower Bucks Lake, just downstream from the much larger Bucks Lake. Campers who seek out the lower lake find a more secluded camping area on the shore of a pretty little lake. Sites are availabelon a first come-first serve basis. Fishing and…
sites.directions: From Quincy, go west on County Road 414, to the intersection with Bucklin Road. Turn right on Bucklin Road and travel approximately 4 miles to Lower Bucks Lake. From Oroville, go east on County Road…
sites.reservations: Sites are available on a first-come, first served basis. Preferred by hunters.

sites.name: Mill Creek (family Campground )
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $31 per night
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from faucets
sites.about: Mill Creek Campground is a small, intimate campground directly on the shore of Bucks Lake. There are 10 sites, two of them are a short walk in and suitable for tent campers. Popular activities at Mill Creek include hiking along the Mill Creek Trail and into the Bucks Lake Wilderness, swimming,…
sites.directions: From Quincy, go west on County Road 414, to the intersection with Bucklin Road. Turn right on Bucklin Road and travel approximately 5 miles to Mill Creek Campground. From Oroville, go east on County…

sites.name: Little Grizzly Creek Campground
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $26 per night
sites.about: Grizzly Creek Campground offers 10 quiet, shady sites amongst the fir trees. It is situated along a feeder stream to Grizzly Creek. It is a short drive (1 mile) to all of the recreational opportunities at Bucks Lake, including swimming, fishing, and hiking.
sites.directions: Located 32 miles northeast of Oroville or 17 miles west of Quincy on the Oro-Quincy Hwy, Grizzly Creek Campground is located one mile west of Bucks Lake.
sites.reservations: Recreation.gov for important information you should know before making your reservation. Sites can be reserved by calling 1-877-444-6777 or online at Recreation.gov .

sites.name: Whitehorse Campground
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $38 per night
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from faucets
sites.about: Whitehorse Campground is located less than 3 miles from Bucks Lake. It has 19 forested sites along Bucks Creek. The Bucks Creek Loop Trail passes through the campground offering hiking and horseback riding from the campground. Three of the sites are available for equestrians.
sites.reservations: Recreation.gov for important information you should know before making your reservation. Sites can be reserved by calling 1-877-444-6777 or online at Recreation.gov .

sites.name: Rock Creek Campground
sites.operator: USDA Forest Service · Plumas National Forest
sites.about: Located in a mixed connifer forest, this campground offers solitude and easy access to the backcountry trails on the Plumas National Forest. All 6 campsites are first come/ first serve. For facility specific information, please call (530) 283-0555.Backcountry roads are easy to explore from this…

sites.name: Silver Lake (Family Campground)
sites.about: Silver Lake Campground provides camping adjacent to Silver Lake, with access to the Bucks Lake Wilderness. The campground provides 9 quiet units for tent camping. Although the campground was burned in the 2021 Dixie Fire, the view of the lake with towering granite peaks in the distance is still…
sites.directions: From Quincy, head west on Bucks Lake Road to Meadow Valley. Turn right on Silver Lake Road. The campground is located 6 miles up at the end of Silver Lake Road.
sites.reservations: 9 sites; no reservations. First come, first served. Recommended for hunters.

sites.name: Grizzly Forebay (Family Campground)
sites.about: GRIZZLY FOREBAY (FAMILY CG) (Campground)

sites.name: Meadow Camp
sites.about: Meadow Camp Campground has streamside campsites with terrific views of both Spanish Peak and Meadow Valley. It has both RV and tent camping and boasts 3 sites for equestrian use. This campground is utilized on a first come - first serve basis. Activities include fishing, birdwatching, hiking,…
sites.directions: Located approximately 10 miles west of Quincy, off of Forest Service Rd 24N29.

sites.name: Little North Fork Campground
sites.feeText: No fees are required for this site
sites.about: 8 developed units located on the Little North Fork of the Middle Fork Feather River. The campground has been recently upgraded with a new vault toilet and potable water system. First come first serve.
sites.accessibility: all units have accessible features, one unit is fully accessible.

sites.name: Deanes Valley Campground
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $15 per night
sites.about: Deanes Valley Campground, located near Meadow Valley, provides seven shady sites along the South Fork of Rock Creek. There is OHV access directly from the campground. The campground accommodates tents and small trailers.
sites.directions: From Quincy, go west on County Road 414. Just before Meadow Valley, turn left (south) on Forest Road 24N28.

sites.name: Rock Creek (Family Campground)
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $15 per night
sites.about: Rock Creek Campground is a small, rustic campground with six sites, all along the edge of the creek. Sites are located on both sides of Rock Creek. It is one of the few campgrounds on the Mt. Hough Ranger District that allows OHV trail access directly from the campground. Other nearby activities…
sites.restrictions: 14 day camping limit. 6 people per campsite. 2 vehicles per campsite. Store food, trash and scented items appropriately - Be Bear Aware.

sites.name: Gansner Bar (family Campground )
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $31 per night
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from faucets
sites.about: Gansner Bar Campground sits along the North Fork of the Feather River. Visitors have access to nearby fishing opportunities. Swimming and tubing are possible when river levels are safe. August is the perfect time to pick blackberries that grow along the river banks.
sites.directions: From Quincy, head west on Hwy 70 for 26 miles. Turn north on Caribou Road. Travel 1 mile to the campground. From Oroville, head east on Hwy 70 for 52 miles. Turn north on Caribou Road. Travel 1 mile…

sites.accessibility: all units have accessible features, one unit is fully accessible.

sites.name: Snake Lake (Family Campground)
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $15 per night
sites.about: SNAKE LAKE (FAMILY CG) (Campground) is located in the Meadow Valley area off of Bucks Lake Road and boasts shady lakeside campsites for tents, RVs, OHVs and horses. It is one of the few campgrounds on the Mt. Hough Ranger District that allows OHV trail access directly from the campground.…

sites.name: Hallsted Campground
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site (Non-Electric): $35 per night Single Site (Electric): $45 per night
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from faucets
sites.about: Hallsted Campground is set amongst large oaks and conifers, providing shady sites along the shore of the beautiful Feather River. A walking path leads from the campground to the river. Visitors will appreciate flush toilets, showers, and electric hook-ups at some sites. There is a general store…
sites.directions: 17 miles west of Quincy along Hwy 70.
sites.reservations: Sites can be reserved online at Recreation.gov or by calling 1-877-444-6777.

sites.about: HANSON CAMP (CUA) (Camping Area)

sites.name: North Fork Campground
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site (Non-Electric): $35 per night Single Site (Electric): $45 per night Dump Station Fee: $17 per use
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from faucets
sites.about: North Fork Campground is located off Caribou Road, along the North Fork of the Feather River. Popular activities include swimming, tubing, and fishing. It is a favorite blackberry picking destination in the late summer months. There are 21 single family campsites, each with a table, fire ring, and…
sites.directions: From Quincy, head west on Hwy 70 for 26 miles. Turn north on Caribou Road. Travel approximately 2 miles to the campground. From Oroville, head east on Hwy 70 for 52 miles. Turn north on Caribou…
sites.reservations: Some sites at this campground are now reservable. To reserve a site please visit visit recreation.gov Recreation.govor call 1-877-444-6777

sites.name: Snake Lake Campground and Equestrian Camp
sites.reservations: No reservations; first come first served. 17 campsites are in the multi-use campground for all campers;. 8 sites have corrals for equestrian campers.
sites.restrictions: Horses allowed overnight in equestrian campsites only. Watering horses at lake edge is prohibited for safety reasons. Water may be bucketed for horses at the spillway. Remove or scatter manure from the corrals and campsites. Please use "weed-seed-free-feed or pellets for horses. 14 day camping…
